seoDescription: Learn how to efficiently manage your Magento 2 products using CSV import/export. This tutorial walks you through creating a new custom product attribute, such as 'laces' for shoes, and assigning it to an attribute set. Discover the process of exporting your product catalog to generate a template CSV, modifying it with new product data, and handling important fields like SKU, URLs, categories, and images. Finally, learn how to import your updated CSV back into Magento, including data validation and troubleshooting common errors.

chapters.title: Introduction to CSV Product Management
chapters.description: This chapter introduces the goal of using CSV for product management and begins the process of creating a new custom 'laces' attribute in Magento 2.

chapters.title: Defining a New Dropdown Attribute
chapters.description: Learn how to define a new product attribute, setting its type to dropdown, adding values like 'Yes' and 'No', and configuring its scope and unique code.

chapters.title: Configuring Attribute Scope and Storefront Properties
chapters.description: Configure the new attribute's scope, labels, and storefront properties, such as its use in search, layered navigation, and promotional rules.

chapters.title: Adding the Attribute to an Attribute Set
chapters.description: Learn how to add the newly created attribute to an attribute set, making it available on the product edit page for data entry.

chapters.title: Creating and Exporting a CSV Template
chapters.description: This section covers manually setting the new attribute for one product to create a complete template, then exporting the entire product catalog to a CSV file.

chapters.title: Analyzing the Exported CSV Structure
chapters.description: A detailed walkthrough of the exported CSV file, explaining key columns like SKU, categories, and price, and noting important rules for unique values and binary (0/1) fields.

chapters.title: Adding a New Product via CSV
chapters.description: Follow along to add a new product to the CSV template, including how to handle image paths for new uploads and locate the 'additional_attributes' column for your custom field.

chapters.title: Importing the CSV File into Magento
chapters.description: Learn the steps to import the modified CSV file into Magento, including selecting import behaviors, choosing the file, and using the 'Check Data' function to validate it before importing.

chapters.title: Troubleshooting and Verifying the Import
chapters.description: See how to diagnose and fix a common import error related to a missing image file, re-import the corrected CSV, and then verify that the new product was successfully created in the Magento backend.

summary:
## Creating a Custom Product Attribute
To add a new piece of information to your products (e.g., whether a shoe has laces), you must first create a custom attribute in Magento.

1.  Navigate to **Stores > Attributes > Product**.
2.  Click **Add New Attribute**.
3.  **Default Label**: Give it a user-friendly name (e.g., "Laces").
4.  **Catalog Input Type**: Choose the field type. For predefined options, use **Dropdown**.
5.  **Values**: Add the options you want (e.g., "Yes" and "No").
6.  **Attribute Code**: Provide a unique, lowercase code (e.g., `laces`).
7.  Configure advanced properties like **Scope** (Global, Website, or Store View) and **Storefront Properties** (use in search, layered navigation, etc.).

## Adding the Attribute to an Attribute Set
An attribute won't appear on a product's edit page until it's added to an attribute set.

1.  Navigate to **Stores > Attributes > Attribute Set**.
2.  Select the set you want to modify (e.g., "Default").
3.  Find your new attribute in the **Unassigned Attributes** list.
4.  Drag and drop it into one of the groups under **Groups** (e.g., "Product Details").
5.  Click **Save**.

## The Export-Modify-Import Workflow
This is the core process for bulk product management via CSV.

1.  **Prepare a Template**: Create or edit at least one product in the Magento admin to have all the attributes and values you need. This makes your export a perfect template.
2.  **Export Products**: Go to **System > Export**, select **Entity Type: Products**, and export the CSV.
3.  **Modify the CSV**: Open the file in a spreadsheet editor (like Google Sheets or Excel). Add new rows for new products or modify existing ones.
4.  **Import Products**: Go to **System > Import**, select **Entity Type: Products**, choose your import behavior (e.g., Add/Update), select your file, and run the import.

> [!TIP]
> Always use the **Check Data** function before importing. It validates your CSV file and reports errors without changing any data, allowing you to fix issues first.

## Key CSV Columns and Rules
- **`sku`**: The Stock Keeping Unit. **Must be unique** for every simple product.
- **`attribute_set_code`**: Must match an existing attribute set in your store (e.g., `Default`).
- **`product_type`**: `simple`, `configurable`, etc.
- **`categories`**: Specify the full path, separated by slashes (e.g., `Default Category/Shoes`).
- **`url_key`**: The URL path for the product. **Must be unique**.
- **Binary Values**: Many fields use `1` for "Yes"/"Enabled" and `0` for "No"/"Disabled" (e.g., `product_online`, `tax_class_id`).
- **`additional_attributes`**: Custom attributes are placed here. The format is `attribute_code=value` (e.g., `laces=Yes`). Separate multiple custom attributes with a comma.

## Handling Product Images
When importing, Magento needs to know where to find the product images.

- **For new images**: Upload your images via FTP/SFTP to a specific folder on your server (e.g., `var/import/images`). In the CSV, just list the filename (e.g., `my-shoe.jpg`). During the import step, you will specify `var/import/images` as the **Images File Directory**.
- **For existing images**: The exported CSV will show a complex path like `/1/5/15.jpg`. This is Magento's internal media storage structure. You can leave these as-is for existing products.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> If your CSV references an image filename but you do not upload that image to the specified directory, the import will fail for that row.
